content.text: Two space buoys X and Y are at rest relative to each other. In the reference frame of the buoys the distance between X and Y is 9.0 × 10⁸ m. A probe travels in a straight line from X to Y at a constant speed of 0.60
What is the time taken for the probe to travel from X to Y as measured by a clock on the probe?
Uses the speed of light instead of the speed of the probe: 9.0 × 10⁸ / 3.00 × 10⁸ = 3.0 s
Applies no relativistic effect; gives the time in the buoys' frame: 5.0 s
Confuses the frame in which the proper time is measured; multiplies by
Time in the buoys' frame = 9.0 × 10⁸ / (0.60 × 3.00 × 10⁸) = 5.0 s. The two events (passing X, passing Y) both occur at the position of the probe; the probe's clock measures the proper time.

content.text: A long space platform has two ends, P and Q. The proper length PQ of the platform is 480 m. A shuttle moves at a constant velocity of 0.80
relative to the platform, parallel to PQ, in the direction from P to Q. The shuttle passes end P (event 1) and later passes end Q (event 2).

content.text: State what is meant by proper length.
the length of an object measured in the reference frame in which the object is at rest
